easy.question: After how many years is there to be a release?
answers: Seven years
Three years
Ten years
easy.explanation: The verse says, “At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release.”

easy.question: What should be done with a brother’s loan in the year of release?
answers: Increase it
Release the debt
Collect it immediately
easy.explanation: The verses command that a brother’s debt be released in the year of release.

easy.question: From whom may the debt be collected, according to the passage?
answers: A brother
Only the poor
A foreigner
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Of a foreigner thou mayest exact it,” while a brother’s debt must be released.

medium.question: Why should a debt not be collected from a brother in the year of release?
answers: Because it is the Lord’s release
Because the brother owes no money
Because the debt is transferred to a foreigner
medium.explanation: The passage says that the debt is not to be collected because the year is the Lord’s release.

medium.question: What is the correct order described in the verses?
answers: First collect from a brother, then release the debt
After seven years comes the year of release, when debts are released
Collect only from foreigners every year
medium.explanation: First the passage announces the release at the end of seven years, then explains that debts are released in that year.

medium.question: In the phrase “Every creditor ... shall release it,” what does “release it” mean?
answers: Give up collecting the debt
Add interest to the debt
Rewrite the debt
medium.explanation: The phrase appears with “he shall not exact it,” so it means giving up the collection of a brother’s debt.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between the treatment of a brother and a foreigner in the year of release?
answers: A debt may not be collected from a brother, but may be collected from a foreigner
More is collected from a brother than from a foreigner
There is no difference
challenge.explanation: The passage makes a clear distinction: a foreigner’s debt may be collected, but a brother’s debt must be released.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “he shall not exact it”?
answers: A brother may not take a loan
The lender may not pressure the brother to repay the debt
The brother must repay before the release begins
challenge.explanation: The phrase means that the lender may not pressure or demand repayment from a brother during the year of release.

challenge.question: What social purpose is suggested by releasing a brother’s debt?
answers: To increase the gap between rich and poor
To encourage rapid debt collection
To ease the burden on a community member who has fallen into debt
challenge.explanation: Releasing the debt and forbidding pressure on the brother are intended to ease his burden during the year of release.

answers: A debt may not be collected from a brother, but may be collected from a foreigner

There is no difference
questions.explanation: The passage makes a clear distinction: a foreigner’s debt may be collected, but a brother’s debt must be released.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “he shall not exact it”?
answers: A brother may not take a loan
The lender may not pressure the brother to repay the debt
The brother must repay before the release begins
questions.explanation: The phrase means that the lender may not pressure or demand repayment from a brother during the year of release.

answers: To increase the gap between rich and poor

easy.question: What will not exist in Israel, according to verse 4?
answers: A poor person
A king
A prophet
easy.explanation: The verse says, “There shall be no poor among you.”

easy.question: What is required of Israel in verse 5?
answers: Build many cities
Listen to the Lord and keep His commandments
Go to war
easy.explanation: The verse requires Israel to listen to the Lord and observe all His commandments.

easy.question: Who will bless Israel, according to the verses?
answers: The nations
Moses
The Lord, Israel’s God
easy.explanation: The blessing is attributed to the Lord: “The Lord thy God blesseth thee.”

medium.question: What is the connection between listening to the Lord and the blessing described in the verses?
answers: Listening to the Lord is presented as a condition for blessing
Listening to the Lord prevents blessing
There is no connection
medium.explanation: The word “Only” presents a condition: the blessing is connected with keeping the commandments.

medium.question: In the phrase “thou shalt lend unto many nations,” what does “lend” mean?
answers: Conquer them in war
Give them money or goods as a loan
Flee from them
medium.explanation: In this context, Israel will lend resources to the nations rather than borrow from them.

medium.question: What is described as a result of the Lord’s blessing of Israel?
answers: Israel will depend on the nations
Israel will leave the land
Israel will lend to nations and rule over many peoples
medium.explanation: Verse 6 says that Israel will lend to the nations, not borrow from them, and will rule over many nations.

challenge.question: What main contrast appears in verse 6 between Israel and the nations?
answers: Israel lends and does not borrow, and rules instead of being ruled
Israel is poor and the nations are rich
Israel serves the nations and the nations serve the Lord
challenge.explanation: The verse presents two contrasts: Israel will lend rather than borrow and rule rather than be ruled.

challenge.question: What does the repetition in “If thou carefully hearken” emphasize?
answers: That one need listen only once
That continual attention and obedience are required
That keeping the commandments is unnecessary
challenge.explanation: The emphatic wording highlights the need to listen carefully and continue observing the commandments.

challenge.question: On what basis is the blessing described in verse 4?
answers: Israel’s military strength
The wealth of the nations
The land the Lord gives Israel as an inheritance
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the blessing with the land the Lord gives Israel as an inheritance.

questions.question: What main contrast appears in verse 6 between Israel and the nations?
answers: Israel lends and does not borrow, and rules instead of being ruled
Israel is poor and the nations are rich
Israel serves the nations and the nations serve the Lord
questions.explanation: The verse presents two contrasts: Israel will lend rather than borrow and rule rather than be ruled.

questions.question: What does the repetition in “If thou carefully hearken” emphasize?
answers: That one need listen only once
That continual attention and obedience are required
That keeping the commandments is unnecessary
questions.explanation: The emphatic wording highlights the need to listen carefully and continue observing the commandments.

questions.question: On what basis is the blessing described in verse 4?
answers: Israel’s military strength
The wealth of the nations
The land the Lord gives Israel as an inheritance
questions.explanation: The verse connects the blessing with the land the Lord gives Israel as an inheritance.

paragraphs.title: Opening the Hand to the Poor

easy.question: To whom are people commanded to open their hands and give help?
answers: A poor brother
Only the king
Only a priest
easy.explanation: The verses command people to help their poor brother and give according to his need.

easy.question: What must a person not do toward his poor brother?
answers: Speak to him
Shut his hand against him
Ask him for advice
easy.explanation: The passage says not to shut one’s hand, meaning not to refuse help to the poor.

easy.question: What does the Lord promise someone who gives generously to the poor?
answers: There will be no poor in the land
He will have a large house
The Lord will bless him in his work
easy.explanation: Verse 10 says that the Lord will bless the giver in all his work.

medium.question: What may happen if someone refuses to give because the year of release is near?
answers: The poor person will move to another city
The poor person will cry to the Lord, and the refusal will be counted as sin
The person will receive double reward
medium.explanation: The verse warns that refusing to give because the year of release is near will cause the poor person to cry to the Lord and will be counted as sin.

medium.question: In “shut thine hand from thy poor brother,” what does “shut thine hand” mean?
answers: Raise your hand
Place your hand on the poor person
Close your hand or refuse to give
medium.explanation: In this context, shutting the hand means refusing to give to the poor.

medium.question: How should the amount of help given to the poor be determined?
answers: According to what he lacks
The exact same amount for everyone
Only if he repays it immediately
medium.explanation: The passage says to give according to what he needs.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “thou shalt open thine hand wide” teach about helping the poor?
answers: Giving once is enough
Giving should be done only in secret
The hand should be opened generously and consistently
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes substantial and generous help rather than a small or reluctant gift.

challenge.question: Why does the Torah say that the poor will never cease from the land?
answers: To explain that there will always be opportunities to practice charity
To excuse people from helping the poor
To announce that all poor people will leave the land
challenge.explanation: Because people in need will always require help, the Torah commands people to keep opening their hands.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the Torah addresses the giver’s inner feelings as well as the act of giving?
answers: The command to give only to a poor person from one’s city
The warning not to let one’s heart be grieved when giving
The promise that all poor people will disappear
challenge.explanation: The Torah requires not only an act of giving but also a willing heart that does not regret the gift.

questions.question: What does the phrase “thou shalt open thine hand wide” teach about helping the poor?
answers: Giving once is enough
Giving should be done only in secret
The hand should be opened generously and consistently
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes substantial and generous help rather than a small or reluctant gift.

questions.question: Why does the Torah say that the poor will never cease from the land?
answers: To explain that there will always be opportunities to practice charity
To excuse people from helping the poor
To announce that all poor people will leave the land
questions.explanation: Because people in need will always require help, the Torah commands people to keep opening their hands.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the Torah addresses the giver’s inner feelings as well as the act of giving?
answers: The command to give only to a poor person from one’s city
The warning not to let one’s heart be grieved when giving
The promise that all poor people will disappear
questions.explanation: The Torah requires not only an act of giving but also a willing heart that does not regret the gift.

paragraphs.title: Releasing a Hebrew Servant and Providing for Him

easy.question: How many years did a Hebrew servant work for his master?
answers: Six years
Seven years
One year
easy.explanation: The verse says that the servant shall serve for six years.

easy.question: When was the servant to be sent free?
answers: In the sixth year
In the seventh year
At the end of the first month
easy.explanation: In the seventh year, the servant was to be released.

easy.question: How must the servant not be sent away?
answers: Without a gift or possessions
Without speaking to him
Only at night
easy.explanation: The passage says not to let him go away empty.

medium.question: What should be done after the servant has worked six years?
answers: Keep him for another year
Send him free and give him a gift
Sell him to someone else
medium.explanation: In the seventh year he is to be released and given provisions rather than sent away empty.

medium.question: In “thou shalt furnish him liberally,” what does “furnish him liberally” mean?
answers: Give him a gift or possessions
Call him back
Punish him
medium.explanation: The context explains that he should receive goods from the flock, the floor, and the winepress.

medium.question: Why does the verse mention the flock, the floor, and the winepress?
answers: To identify sources from which the servant should be provided
To forbid raising animals
To determine where he must work
medium.explanation: The verse lists the possessions from which the servant is to be given provisions when released.

challenge.question: What social principle can be inferred from calling the servant “thy brother”?
answers: He should be treated with respect and responsibility
His needs may be ignored
He must work without limits
challenge.explanation: Calling him a brother presents him as part of the community and emphasizes humane, responsible treatment.

challenge.question: What is the connection between remembering the Exodus and releasing the servant?
answers: Those redeemed from slavery should act generously toward their servants
The Exodus cancels the duty to release servants
Only someone who lived in Egypt may be a servant
challenge.explanation: The passage recalls that the Israelites were slaves and were redeemed, so they must release and assist their servant.

challenge.question: What can be understood from giving the servant goods “wherewith the Lord thy God hath blessed thee”?
answers: Giving comes from the blessing the master has received
Only money may be given
The servant must repay the gift
challenge.explanation: The verse connects God’s blessing with the master’s duty to share his possessions with the departing servant.

questions.question: What social principle can be inferred from calling the servant “thy brother”?
answers: He should be treated with respect and responsibility
His needs may be ignored
He must work without limits
questions.explanation: Calling him a brother presents him as part of the community and emphasizes humane, responsible treatment.

questions.question: What is the connection between remembering the Exodus and releasing the servant?
answers: Those redeemed from slavery should act generously toward their servants
The Exodus cancels the duty to release servants
Only someone who lived in Egypt may be a servant
questions.explanation: The passage recalls that the Israelites were slaves and were redeemed, so they must release and assist their servant.

questions.question: What can be understood from giving the servant goods “wherewith the Lord thy God hath blessed thee”?
answers: Giving comes from the blessing the master has received
Only money may be given
The servant must repay the gift
questions.explanation: The verse connects God’s blessing with the master’s duty to share his possessions with the departing servant.

paragraphs.title: A Servant Who Chooses to Stay

easy.question: What does the servant say to his master?
answers: I will not go away from you
I will return home immediately
I will work for only one year
easy.explanation: The servant says, “I will not go away from thee,” because he loves his master and his household.

easy.question: What does the master do to a servant who chooses to stay?
answers: Give him gifts only
Pierce his ear at the door
Send him free
easy.explanation: The passage says to take an awl and thrust it through his ear unto the door.

easy.question: What is the servant called after this act?
answers: A one-year servant
A hired worker
A servant forever
easy.explanation: The passage says that he will be the master’s servant forever.

medium.question: Why does the servant not want to leave?
answers: Because he loves his master and his household
Because he is afraid of the journey
Because he wants to work six more years
medium.explanation: The servant says he remains because he loves his master and household and is well with them.

medium.question: What is an awl, in the phrase “thou shalt take an awl”?
answers: A sharp tool for piercing
The servant’s garment
A gift for the master
medium.explanation: An awl is a sharp tool, as shown by its use to pierce the servant’s ear.

medium.question: What does the Torah command when the time comes to release the servant?
answers: Leave him at home without deciding
Send him free without regret
Pierce his ear immediately
medium.explanation: The passage says that it should not seem hard to send him free after six years of service.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “he hath been worth a double hired servant to thee”?
answers: The servant worked for a long period and deserved fair treatment
The servant worked only half the time
The servant received double pay every day
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes six years of service and therefore calls for generous, considerate treatment at his release.

challenge.question: What does “And also unto thy maidservant thou shalt do likewise” teach?
answers: The command applies only to male servants
The same treatment applies to a female servant
The female servant must remain forever
challenge.explanation: The verse adds that the same rule applies to a maidservant who chooses to remain.

challenge.question: What sequence of events is described in the verses?
answers: The servant is freed, asks to stay, and then begins working
The servant asks to stay, is pierced, and becomes a servant forever
The master frees the servant, sells him, and then blesses him
challenge.explanation: First the servant asks to remain, then his ear is pierced, and finally he becomes a servant forever.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “he hath been worth a double hired servant to thee”?
answers: The servant worked for a long period and deserved fair treatment
The servant worked only half the time
The servant received double pay every day
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes six years of service and therefore calls for generous, considerate treatment at his release.

questions.question: What does “And also unto thy maidservant thou shalt do likewise” teach?
answers: The command applies only to male servants
The same treatment applies to a female servant
The female servant must remain forever
questions.explanation: The verse adds that the same rule applies to a maidservant who chooses to remain.

questions.question: What sequence of events is described in the verses?
answers: The servant is freed, asks to stay, and then begins working
The servant asks to stay, is pierced, and becomes a servant forever
The master frees the servant, sells him, and then blesses him
questions.explanation: First the servant asks to remain, then his ear is pierced, and finally he becomes a servant forever.

paragraphs.title: Consecrating the Firstborn of Herds and Flocks

easy.question: What must be consecrated to the Lord?
answers: Every firstborn male
All the cattle
The oldest sheep
easy.explanation: The passage commands that every firstborn male of the herd and flock be sanctified to the Lord.

easy.question: What must not be done with the firstborn of an ox?
answers: Eat it
Work it
Bring it to the chosen place
easy.explanation: The passage says not to do work with the firstborn of the ox.

easy.question: Who may eat the firstborn animal?
answers: Only the priests
Only the owner of the herd
You and your household
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thou and thy household.”

medium.question: What is the correct order described in the verses?
answers: Consecrate the firstborn, then eat it before the Lord
Eat the firstborn, then consecrate it
Work the firstborn, then shear it
medium.explanation: First the animal is consecrated to the Lord; afterward it is eaten before Him at the chosen place.

medium.question: Why must the firstborn ox not be used for work or the firstborn sheep be sheared?
answers: Because they are too young
Because they are consecrated to the Lord
Because raising cattle and sheep is forbidden
medium.explanation: The firstborn male is dedicated to the Lord, so it may not be used for work or wool.

medium.question: In “nor shear the firstling of thy sheep,” what does “shear” mean?
answers: Slaughter
Sell
Cut off the wool
medium.explanation: To shear a sheep is to cut off its wool; the passage forbids doing this to the firstborn.

challenge.question: What precise detail appears in the command about the firstborn?
answers: It applies to the firstborn male
It applies only to females
It applies to every offspring
challenge.explanation: The passage specifically says “firstling males,” so the command concerns male firstborn animals.

challenge.question: What can be understood from “year by year”?
answers: It is eaten only once in a lifetime
The eating takes place every year
It may be eaten every day
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates a recurring yearly practice at the place the Lord chooses.

challenge.question: What is the correct relationship between the two verses?
answers: The first concerns only the Temple, and the second concerns fieldwork
The first permits shearing, and the second forbids eating
The first establishes the firstborn’s holiness, and the second explains how and where it is eaten
challenge.explanation: The first verse establishes the animal’s consecration and forbids using it; the second describes eating it before the Lord at the chosen place.

questions.question: What precise detail appears in the command about the firstborn?
answers: It applies to the firstborn male
It applies only to females
It applies to every offspring
questions.explanation: The passage specifically says “firstling males,” so the command concerns male firstborn animals.

questions.question: What can be understood from “year by year”?
answers: It is eaten only once in a lifetime
The eating takes place every year
It may be eaten every day
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates a recurring yearly practice at the place the Lord chooses.

questions.question: What is the correct relationship between the two verses?
answers: The first concerns only the Temple, and the second concerns fieldwork
The first permits shearing, and the second forbids eating
The first establishes the firstborn’s holiness, and the second explains how and where it is eaten
questions.explanation: The first verse establishes the animal’s consecration and forbids using it; the second describes eating it before the Lord at the chosen place.

paragraphs.title: A Firstborn with a Defect and the Prohibition on Eating Blood

easy.question: What should be done with an animal that has a defect?
answers: It must not be sacrificed to the Lord
It must be sacrificed immediately
It must be released into the wilderness
easy.explanation: The passage says not to sacrifice an animal that has a blemish.

easy.question: Where may an animal with a defect be eaten?
answers: Only at the Temple
Within your gates
Only in the wilderness
easy.explanation: Instead of sacrificing it, the animal may be eaten within the gates.

easy.question: Which part of the animal must not be eaten?
answers: The meat
The hide
The blood
easy.explanation: The passage specifically says, “Only thou shalt not eat the blood thereof.”

medium.question: What may be done with an animal that has a defect?
answers: It may be eaten within the gates by the unclean and the clean
It may be sacrificed only during a festival
Only the priests may eat it
medium.explanation: Although it may not be sacrificed, it may be eaten within the gates by both the unclean and the clean.

medium.question: What does “blemish” mean in “if there be any blemish therein”?
answers: A special color
A physical defect or injury
A young age
medium.explanation: The passage explains a blemish with examples such as being lame or blind.

medium.question: What sequence of actions is described in the verses?
answers: Eat the blood, sacrifice the animal, then pour out the meat
Sacrifice the animal, eat it within the gates, then drink its blood
Do not sacrifice the animal, eat it within the gates, and pour out its blood
medium.explanation: First the animal may not be sacrificed; then it may be eaten; finally, its blood must not be eaten but poured out.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “the unclean and the clean person shall eat it alike”?
answers: Eating this animal is not limited to a ritually clean person
Only an unclean person may eat it
No one may eat it
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that both the unclean and the clean may eat it together.

challenge.question: Why is the animal compared with “the roebuck and the hart”?
answers: To say that it must be a wild animal
To emphasize that it is eaten as ordinary meat, not as a sacrifice
To teach that its meat may not be eaten
challenge.explanation: The comparison emphasizes ordinary eating of meat rather than eating a sacrifice at the sanctuary.

challenge.question: What important difference is there between the animal’s meat and its blood?
answers: The blood may be eaten but the meat may not
Neither the meat nor the blood may be eaten
The meat may be eaten, but the blood may not be eaten and must be poured on the ground
challenge.explanation: The meat may be eaten within the gates, but the blood remains forbidden and must be poured out.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “the unclean and the clean person shall eat it alike”?
answers: Eating this animal is not limited to a ritually clean person
Only an unclean person may eat it
No one may eat it
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says that both the unclean and the clean may eat it together.

questions.question: Why is the animal compared with “the roebuck and the hart”?
answers: To say that it must be a wild animal
To emphasize that it is eaten as ordinary meat, not as a sacrifice
To teach that its meat may not be eaten
questions.explanation: The comparison emphasizes ordinary eating of meat rather than eating a sacrifice at the sanctuary.

questions.question: What important difference is there between the animal’s meat and its blood?
answers: The blood may be eaten but the meat may not
Neither the meat nor the blood may be eaten
The meat may be eaten, but the blood may not be eaten and must be poured on the ground
questions.explanation: The meat may be eaten within the gates, but the blood remains forbidden and must be poured out.
